subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: Should OpenClaw implement a core framework-level plugin circuit breaker, and what plugin API, storage owner, operator controls, and default fail modes should it use?
rationale: The remaining work adds new runtime policy, state, status/reset surfaces, and compatibility-sensitive plugin behavior that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Core Breaker Contract First
options.body: Keep this open for a maintainer-led design covering hook attribution, SQLite-backed state, status/reset commands, passive telemetry, and compatibility-safe defaults before implementation.

options.title: Keep Breakers Plugin-Owned
options.body: Close or narrow this request and ask high-risk plugins to implement degradation through existing plugin-local config and runtime state surfaces.

options.title: Ship Passive Telemetry First
options.body: Implement timing/failure counters and status visibility only, then decide active open/half-open quarantine behavior after deployment evidence.

recommendation.title: Design Core Breaker Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this open for a maintainer-led design covering hook attribution, SQLite-backed state, status/reset commands, passive telemetry, and compatibility-safe defaults before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans runtime state, gateway operator controls, and compatibility policy, areas where recent merged history points to steipete as the strongest available routing candidate.
